### 1. What the customer states, and what the simulator may do

From `user_scenario`: Franklin K. Osei-Boateng rings *"about one thing only, and he says it plainly: 'When it's finished I'd like it posted out to me rather than having to come in and collect it. I've had a knee replaced and I'm not driving for a while yet. Can that be arranged?'"*

- Target object: his mother's Edwardian diamond-and-platinum brooch, left at the Sacramento store *"at the end of August"*. He **cannot quote a work order number** — *"He does not have the paperwork in front of him and he cannot quote a work order number."* The object must be found from the records.
- Timing: no deadline; *"He is not in a hurry and he does not ask what anything costs."*
- Boundary of the action: he wants the piece posted rather than collected; he accepts the postage charge once told — *"that's fine, put it on the bill"* — and *"asks nothing about how it was worked out."*
- Mode of authorisation: he performs the customer-side step himself — *"If the agent tells him that before the bench can go any further he has to put his name to something that records what the brooch is held at while the chain has it, he asks what figure that will say, listens to the answer, and then agrees; when the agent passes that step across to him he does it himself and repeats back what it says."*
- The simulator is passive and conditional: phone `4155553352` offered for finding him; date of birth `1957-11-09` only *"if more is wanted"*; identification last four `3318` only *"if that is still not enough"*; *"He will not volunteer all of it at once; he answers what he is asked."* He explicitly refuses to read out the estate valuation figure — *"he will not read it out over the telephone and says the store will have its own record of it"* — so the appraisal figure must come from the records, not from him. Coverage and membership are confirmed only if asked, without numbers. He never names a tool, a policy or a next step.

### 4. Each scored parameter, in words, with inputs, intermediates and value

Heritage Restoration Service level figures: insured shipping rate **55.00** per leg; shipping insurance ceiling 50,000.00; target turnaround **25 business days**; rush turnaround **12 business days**; stone release threshold **5,000.00**; care and custody cover cap **100,000.00**; estimate validity 60 days; member discount 10 %.

**(A) The value the piece is carried at — `carried_value`.**
Computation document: `carried_value_basis_and_cover_cap_share_50a2d47b` — *"The value is the basis figure taken with the steps that bear on it added, and it is never more than the level's own care and custody cover cap taken at the evidenced share; the figure is rounded to the nearest cent."*

| Input | Tier taken and the return that put it there | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Basis figure | `basis_figure_from_an_appraisal_report_9967013e` cl. 1 — an appraisal report stands on the piece (`4bd5ce7c-…`, `item_sku='BRCH-19044'`, delivered) and is still current, `valid_until='2028-04-18'` being later than 2026-09-25 → *"the basis figure is the value that report states"* = `appraised_value` | **12,400.00** (not the counter figure 6,800.00) |
| Cover step | `cover_step_for_coverage_in_force_9d43bf8e` row 2 — coverage in force (`status='active'`, `expiry_date=''`) and a claim settled against it (`claims_settled_count=1`; ledger `e5834068-…` `protection_claim_settled` `settled_full`) → reduced cover step | **+8 %** |
| Holding step | `holding_step_for_long_held_and_part_paid_pieces_b794934a` row *(no, yes)* — `intake_date='2026-08-31'` → 25 calendar days, against the level's target 25 business days = 35 calendar days, so **not** longer; and a payment stands on the order (`36f556f6-…`, −2,100.00) → standing holding step | **+4 %** |
| Evidenced share of the cover cap | `evidenced_share_of_the_custody_cover_cap_b73e74e1` cl. 1 — a current appraisal report stands **and** coverage stands in force → *"the whole of the cover cap, 100 percent of it"* | **100 % of 100,000.00** |

12,400.00 × (100 % + 8 % + 4 %) = 12,400.00 × 1.12 = **13,888.00**. Cap at the evidenced share = 100,000.00. Lower of the two = **13,888.00**.
Call: `confirm_stone_release_3a8d360e{service_order_id='3df43144-…', customer_id='58974075-…', carried_value=13888.00}`, run **by the customer**.

**(B) The insured shipping charge — `shipping_amount`.**
Computation document: `insured_return_charge_on_the_level_rate_ebe6f9b7` — *"charged on the level's own insured shipping rate, taken with the steps that bear on the leg added and the step for a leg already travelled taken off, and with the relief a member is allowed applied; every figure is rounded to the nearest cent."* The rate *"enters at the whole of itself, 100 percent, and the steps that bear on the leg are added to that whole and the step for a leg already travelled taken off it."*

| Input | Tier taken and the return that put it there | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Level rate | `insured_shipping_rates_and_appraisal_updates_ea159517`, Heritage Restoration Service column | **55.00** |
| Value step | `value_step_on_insured_return_for_covered_pieces_64f3d657` cl. 1 — the value the piece is held at, 13,888.00 from step A, at or above the price the covered piece was sold at (`item_value_at_purchase=9600.0`), coverage in force → upper value step | **+45 %** |
| Promise proximity step | `promise_proximity_step_on_insured_return_f0775a23` cl. 2 — `promised_date='2026-10-16'` is 21 calendar days from the handling date; the level's rush turnaround 12 business days = 16.8 calendar days (21 is **not** inside it), the target 25 business days = 35 calendar days (21 **is** inside it) → standard promise step | **+18 %** |
| Paperwork step | `paperwork_step_for_appraisal_papers_travelling_with_a_piece_2f166e25` cl. 1 — the engagement on the piece has been delivered and its report is still current at the handling date → report paperwork step | **+12 %** |
| Step off for legs already charged | `step_off_for_insured_legs_already_charged_ccce9c0f` row 2 — exactly one insured leg already stands charged **on that work order** (`c6b2433a-…`, `shipping_insured`, 55.00, 2026-09-01); the 18.00 leg belongs to the other order and *"the leg now being charged is not among them"* → return-leg step | **−15 %** |
| Relief allowed | `member_relief_on_insured_return_charges_26d10098` cl. 2 — membership active; qualifying workshop spend on `workshop_service` entries in the twelve months to 2026-09-25 (window opens 2025-09-25) = 2,100.00 only (the 640.00 entry is dated 2025-08-14, outside the window), below the 2,500 threshold → standing relief | **12 %** |
| Where the relief is taken off | `where_member_relief_is_taken_off_insured_return_charges_72f83480` row 1 — membership active and a member benefit drawn in the window (`circle_benefit_redeemed` 2026-03-02, `complimentary_appraisal`) → *"off the whole charge once every step has been applied"* | — |

Multiplier = 100 % + 45 % + 18 % + 12 % − 15 % = 160 %. 55.00 × 1.60 = **88.00**. Relief off the whole: 88.00 × (1 − 12 %) = **77.44**.
(Cross-check against the document's own worked example, which takes a 40.00 rate with a 45 % step and 25 % relief to 58.00 then 43.50 — the same order of operations.)

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**The customer named one problem**: post the brooch out instead of collecting it.

**Hop 1 — the postage charge waits on a signed release naming the value (state-derived).**
`insured_return_of_a_piece_from_the_bench_28739b12` states, in the blocked policy's own rule: *"The charge for sending the piece back is worked out only after the work order carries a signed release naming the value the piece is held at."* A record-visible state of the work order, not an action, and not a named performer. Checking the records: the order shows `stone_release_signed=False`, and the only workshop request on file, `a8786093-…`, is `request_type='stone_release_consent'` with `request_status='recorded'` — taken down, not signed. **The state does not hold.** Searching with the words the sentence and the records use — "release", "signed", "the value the piece is held at" — reaches `stone_release_and_the_value_a_piece_is_carried_at_56cb0175`, which describes the write that brings the state about: *"One call marks the release as signed on the named work order and writes onto that same order the value the piece is held at while the chain has it, replacing whatever figure was taken down over the counter"*, and *"Once the release stands signed, the work order shows both the signed release and the agreed figure."* The same words reach the base clause `intake_admission_and_stone_release_86e1df81` cl. 2, which independently confirms that this piece needs one: *"A piece whose declared value exceeds the level's stone release threshold is worked on only once the customer has signed the stone release, and their saying they are happy for the bench to proceed is not the signed release"* — `declared_value=6800.0` against a Heritage Restoration threshold of 5,000.00. The figure to be named is worked in `carried_value_basis_and_cover_cap_share_50a2d47b`. **Mark: state-derived.**

**Hop 2 — nothing further.** `stone_release_and_the_value_a_piece_is_carried_at_56cb0175` states no prerequisite sentence of its own, and every input the carried value needs (the appraisal report, the coverage, the intake date, the payment) stands on the records already. The recursion terminates.

**Resulting tree and handling order.**
```
sign the release naming the carried value   (customer's own write, unnamed by the customer)
        ↓ brings about: "the work order carries a signed release naming the value the piece is held at"
price the insured postage leg               (the only thing the customer asked about)
```
Direction: postage → release. Handling order: release, then postage. The one hop is **state-derived**; **no hop was pre-solved** — `insured_return_of_a_piece_from_the_bench_28739b12` names only its own tool and never names the release tool, the resolving problem or an order of work.

### Two-way counter-proof

**(i) The visible materials fully support the conclusion.** Every figure traces to a quoted document sentence plus a quoted record field.

**(ii) The closest alternative on each boundary is excluded by a visible sentence or record.**

| Closest alternative | What excludes it |
|---|---|
| Take the basis figure from the counter (`declared_value=6800.0`) | `basis_figure_from_an_appraisal_report_9967013e` cl. 1 takes the report's figure where the report is current, and `carried_value_basis_and_cover_cap_share_50a2d47b` says the value is worked *"from the papers standing on the piece rather than from the figure taken down over the counter"* |
| Read clause 2 of the basis rule (greater of report and counter) | Clause 2 applies only *"where an appraisal report … has run out"*; `valid_until='2028-04-18'` has not |
| Charge per leg at the level rate, 55.00 flat | `payment_shipping_and_appraisal_updates_fa15c13e` records *"The condition that insured shipping is charged per leg at the level's rate is **no longer in force**"* and points to the current basis |
| Count the 18.00 insured leg of 2026-02-18 among the legs already charged | `step_off_for_insured_legs_already_charged_ccce9c0f`: the count is *"the insured shipping legs already standing charged on that work order"*; that leg stands on `01609447-…` |
| Treat the promised date as inside the rush turnaround (40 % step) | 12 business days convert to 16.8 calendar days by the document's own 7-to-5 rule, and 2026-10-16 is 21 days out |
| Treat the piece as held longer than the target (9 % holding step) | 25 calendar days since `intake_date` against a 35 calendar-day equivalent of the level's 25 business days |
| Give the high 25 % relief | `member_relief_on_insured_return_charges_26d10098` sets the threshold at 2,500 qualifying workshop spend; only 2,100.00 falls in the window |
| Take the relief off the value step alone | `where_member_relief_is_taken_off_insured_return_charges_72f83480` row 1 applies, a `circle_benefit_redeemed` row standing within the window |
| Refuse to ship | The value carried, 13,888.00, is inside the level's 50,000.00 shipping insurance ceiling |
| Treat the `recorded` consent request as the release | `intake_admission_and_stone_release_86e1df81`: *"their saying they are happy for the bench to proceed is not the signed release … the release is shown by the record standing against that work order reference"*, and the order reads `stone_release_signed=False` |

**(iii) The natural wrong answer — "he asked only to have it posted, so only post it" — is excluded.** Charging the postage line now would price it while the work order carries no signed release naming the value the piece is held at, which `insured_return_of_a_piece_from_the_bench_28739b12` forbids in terms (*"only after"*). It is further excluded by an independent base clause: the piece's declared value of 6,800.00 exceeds the level's 5,000.00 stone release threshold, so by `intake_admission_and_stone_release_86e1df81` cl. 2 the piece may not be worked on at all until the release is signed. Both exclusions are prerequisite/base sentences on the blocked side — no route, no tool name, no chain.

**(iv) The fall-back number for the computation is definite and different.** Reading `insured_return_charge_on_the_level_rate_ebe6f9b7` alone with the product figure it names, and applying no factor: the level's own insured shipping rate for Heritage Restoration Service, no step added, no step taken off, no relief = **55.00 USD**. Definite, and different from 77.44. Likewise the carried value with no factor: basis = the value the piece was taken in at, 6,800.00; steps none; cover cap 100,000.00 at the narrow evidenced share of 10 % = 10,000.00; lower of the two = 6,800.00.

**(v) How each factor document was reached from the customer's own records.**

| Factor document | The record words that led to it |
|---|---|
| `basis_figure_from_an_appraisal_report_9967013e` | the appraisal engagement standing on `item_sku='BRCH-19044'` with an `appraised_value` and a `valid_until` date — the customer's own statement that *"his mother's estate had it valued after she died"* points at the same record |
| `cover_step_for_coverage_in_force_9d43bf8e` | the protection plan standing `active` on that sku with `claims_settled_count=1` |
| `holding_step_for_long_held_and_part_paid_pieces_b794934a` | the order's `intake_date` and the `service_payment_received` row (he says he *"paid something towards it that day on his card"*) |
| `evidenced_share_of_the_custody_cover_cap_b73e74e1` | the appraisal engagement's currency and the plan's standing |
| `value_step_on_insured_return_for_covered_pieces_64f3d657` | the plan's `item_value_at_purchase` against the value the order now holds the piece at |
| `promise_proximity_step_on_insured_return_f0775a23` | the order's `promised_date='2026-10-16'` |
| `paperwork_step_for_appraisal_papers_travelling_with_a_piece_2f166e25` | the appraisal engagement's `status='delivered'` and its `valid_until` |
| `step_off_for_insured_legs_already_charged_ccce9c0f` | the `shipping_insured` row already standing on this work order |

All reachable through the words the records use; none required phrasing borrowed from the computation document, and neither computation document announced that a variation existed.

### No divergence found

Every scored value, every tier, every object boundary, every owner, the whole tool sequence and the single prerequisite hop are entailed by the visible materials alone and equal the source layer. Both of this task's computations are rounding-stable: 12,400.00 × 1.12 = 13,888.00 and 55.00 × 1.60 = 88.00 → × 0.88 = 77.44 are exact at the cent under any rounding mode, so the defect recorded against task 0 does not reach this task.

The two-way counter-proof in `blind_answer` also held against the source: each boundary the visible corpus closes (the report's currency for the basis figure, the leg count scoped to this work order, the 16.8 / 35 calendar-day conversions, the 2,500 relief threshold, the member-benefit window) is closed by the source in the same place and at the same strength, and no boundary the source leaves open is closed by a document.

### Verdict

**PASS** (runtime blind audit) for task 1.
